worked_solution:
We start by integrating the velocity to get $x(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & =\int v(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int (8{t}^{3}+12)\,\text{d}t \\  & =8\cdot \frac{{t}^{4}}{4}+12t+C \\  & =2{t}^{4}+12t+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C$, we use the fact that $x(1)=10.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}10 & =2(1)^{4}+12(1)+C \\ 10 & =2+12+C \\ C & =-4.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the position $x$ of the particle at time $t$ is 

$$
x(t)=2{t}^{4}+12t-4.
$$
